title: Bulgari Rome vs Corinthia Rome: The Two Big-Room Hotels (2026) | Suites With Keith
description: Bulgari Hotel Roma vs Corinthia Rome, compared by a travel advisor who visited both in October 2026: room sizes, lively or quiet, spa and gym, dining, design, and who each one suits.

hero.alt: The Bulgari Hotel Roma rooftop at sunset, a brick walkway under green arches lined with lounge seating
A Corinthia Rome suite with double-height windows, a gilded mirror over the sofa and a marble table

sub: Space is rare in central Rome, and these are the two exceptions I found. Both have a spa. The difference is the mood. Here is how I would choose.

choose.h3: If you want energy and great dining
choose.lead: Spectacular. Base rooms the size of junior suites elsewhere, marble and mosaics, a lively, sophisticated scene, more bars and restaurants than I could count, and the biggest gym in Rome.
choose.alt: The entry hall of a Bulgari Hotel Roma room, with wood-paneled wardrobes and an oak floor

choose.h3: If you want to come home to quiet
choose.lead: Wow. A showstopper renovation, large rooms and a beautiful spa, across from parliament: incredibly safe, and quiet while still in the middle of everything.
choose.alt: A Corinthia Rome bedroom with a bronze canopy bed and a terrace draped in bougainvillea

band.h2: Both give you space. Do you want a buzz with it, or quiet?
paras: The Bulgari is lively, almost like an EDITION but much more sophisticated, with more places to eat and drink than I could count. If you want quiet and calm, it is not the one.

The Corinthia is across the street from parliament, so the area is incredibly safe, and quiet while still being in the middle of everything. I was blown away. I think it is truly a game changer for Rome.
If you want to stay in for dinner, drinks and a workout, pick the Bulgari. If you want a calm base and a beautiful spa, pick the Corinthia.

guide.alt: A Bulgari Hotel Roma base room with a tall upholstered headboard and round brass reading lights
paras: The Bulgari’s base rooms are what other hotels would sell as a deluxe room or a junior suite, so the entry rate already buys real space. You often don’t need to upgrade.
The Corinthia’s rooms are large and tastefully appointed, and some bedrooms open onto terraces. It is new, so room categories and views vary. Book with someone who knows it.

guide.alt: The Bulgari Hotel Roma gym, with racks, benches and plates against warm wood paneling
paras: If you train on vacation, the Bulgari has the biggest gym I saw in Rome, massive and with serious equipment, plus a spa.
The Corinthia’s spa is beautiful, as are its public spaces, which are big enough that the hotel never feels crowded.

guide.alt: A Bulgari Hotel Roma terrace table under a white umbrella at sunset, looking over trees and rooftops
paras: At the Bulgari, there is a beautiful rooftop bar and pizza restaurant, another bar on the floor below it, and more. Downstairs there’s a classic Roman trattoria with fair prices, like €18 pastas. I loved that.
At the Corinthia, the draw is the renovation and the calm. Being central and quiet means the city’s restaurants are a short walk away.

guide.alt: A Corinthia Rome bathroom in onyx and marble, with a freestanding stone tub and a crystal chandelier
paras: The Corinthia’s renovation is a showstopper from the moment you walk in, down to the onyx and marble bathrooms.
The Bulgari is very modern, with lots of marble and incredible mosaics in the bathrooms. It sits right next to the Mausoleum of Augustus, which is almost done with its renovation.

faq.q: Which is better, the Bulgari or the Corinthia?
faq.a: Both give you space, which is rare in central Rome. The Bulgari for energy, great dining in the hotel and the biggest gym in Rome. The Corinthia for quiet, a beautiful spa and a showstopper renovation.
The Corinthia, across the street from parliament. The Bulgari is on the lively side, and you step out into busy streets.
Both are among the few central Rome hotels where space is the story. At the Bulgari, the entry rooms are the value. At the Corinthia, the rooms are large, and I’ll steer you to the right category.

faq.q: Which has the better spa and gym?
faq.a: For a gym, the Bulgari: the biggest I saw in Rome. For a beautiful spa in a calm hotel, the Corinthia.

faq.q: Which is better for a couple wanting quiet?
faq.a: The Corinthia. If you want quiet and calm, the Bulgari is not the one I’d pick. The Eden, my top pick in Rome, is the other quiet option.
